Subject: Pricing & monthly commit smoothing for upcoming holiday ramp

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We confirmed internal approval for a hosted-API pilot that will spike during our November–January launch window, then moderate through Q2 with a predictable seasonal drop. I attached our month-by-month forecast so you can see the shape.

Ask: can Redwood provide a step-up monthly commit schedule (we want to gradually increase committed spend month-over-month for the first six months) and a smoothing mechanism that prevents punitive true-ups in off-season months? Specifically: can we get a per-token rate matrix tied to commit tiers, a surge buffer for launch weeks, and an off-season credit (or smoothing) that applies when usage drops below forecast?

Constraints: procurement requires clear monthly billing, a one-line SOW, and a DocuSign-ready contract. We prefer monthly true-ups over quarterly if possible.

Attachment: stratus_monthly_forecast.csv (csv, 42KB)

Hi Anna — really helpful context and thanks for the forecast.

High level summary of what we can offer immediately:
- Monthly step-up commits: commit tiers that increase month-over-month for a 6-month ramp. We will model a baseline commit and then a planned increment each month (e.g., 50M tokens -> 100M -> 175M).
- Per-token tiered pricing: lower per-token unit price as you hit higher commit tiers. See attached matrix (xlsx) for example rates and effective token-price at 50%, 75%, 100% of commit.
- Surge buffer: a small reserved pool we keep for launch weeks to avoid immediate overage charges (configurable, default 20% of the committed month).
- Off-season smoothing: two options we can offer — (A) monthly true-up with a capped off-season credit up to X% (we recommend 10–15% cap), or (B) a rolling 3-month smoothing window for true-ups to average usage and reduce volatility.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus and Laura will propose the exact numbers for the per-token matrix and smoothing caps (attached).
2) We prepare a one-page SOW + DocuSign envelope for procurement with the pricing from the attached matrix.
3) If that looks good, sign and pick a start date — we'll honor the surge buffer for the first two months of the ramp.

Attachment: redwood_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)

Anna / Olga — quick internal pricing note and recommended structure below.

I ran the forecast attached to several tier shapes. Our recommended option balances predictability for Stratus and revenue protection for Redwood:

- Commit tiers (monthly):
  * Tier A: 0–50M tokens -> $0.00030 / token (baseline)
  * Tier B: 50M–150M tokens -> $0.00022 / token
  * Tier C: 150M–400M tokens -> $0.00016 / token

- Step-up schedule (example months 1–6): 50M -> 85M -> 130M -> 200M -> 260M -> 320M
- Surge buffer: default 20% of committed month. Overages within buffer billed at mid-tier rate (effective ≈ 10–15% surcharge vs committed tier).
- Off-season smoothing: monthly true-up with a cap credit up to 15% for months where usage < 60% of forecasted commit OR an alternative rolling 3-month average true-up (we can make this a selectable clause in the SOW).
- True-up cadence: monthly invoices, with final reconciliation at quarter end; if you prefer monthly-only reconciliation we can adjust (qtrs are standard but monthly is workable for deals < $100k/mo).

Sample math (month 4): committed 200M tokens, actual usage 120M (60% of commit). Under monthly true-up with 15% off-season credit cap:
- Raw shortfall = 80M tokens * baseline price at committed tier = $0.00016 -> $12,800 shortfall
- Off-season credit applied = min(15% of shortfall, negotiated floor) -> credit approx $1,920 -> net shortfall billed $10,880

Legal/procurement notes: add a clause allowing a one-time adjustment in month 2 if onboarding-generated traffic is materially different (>30% variance) so early launch volatility doesn't penalize you.

If that looks good I can prepare the DocuSign-ready SOW and pricing attachment.

Marcus Lin
